cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Could You Just…
cards.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you hold my bouquet stems together? Keep the flower heads level, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're level. You need wire under that ribbon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, a concealed binding. Could you twist this piece once, just below your fingers? Keep it tight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done, but the end will catch on the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tuck it inward, please. Just wind the ribbon over it and tie one small bow. Small, please; the bride is carrying flowers, not ribbon.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 wire idea leads to A3 twist; B4 snag leads to A5 tuck and full ribbon finish, with size now specified prospectively.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 supply competent help and identify real defects; A keeps expanding what the helper must do.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 sharp wire into completing the wrap and bow, most of the task A originally needed help with.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 flowers-not-ribbon distinction directly explains the requested small bow to B, rather than describing the card mechanism.
